To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the spinal cord circuitry responsible for locomotion can also control the activity of respiratory neurons engaged in the expiratory phase of breathing.
the locomotor central pattern generator for hindlimb control modulates the activity of respiratory neurons in the spinal cord of newborn rats.
the central pattern generator for respiration and the central pattern generator of locomotion are connected by excitatory spinal neurons that are active only during expiration.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the neural bases for the coordination of rhythmic motor patterns in the neonatal rat spinal cord and brainstem.
understanding the mechanisms underlying the coordination of the neural circuitry responsible to generate rhythmic motor outputs in different motor behaviors.

In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

this work provides a first evidence in the neonatal rat spinal cord for bimodal respiratory–locomotor neurons and interneurons, onto which central efferent respiratory and locomotor drives can converge, presumably facilitating coordination between the respiratory and locomotor networks.
the respiratory neurons engaged in the expiratory phase are rhythmically modulated by the locomotor network, whereas those involved in the inspiratory phase are not.
the respiratory and locomotor circuits interact to coordinate their activities.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the locomotor signal is able to influence the respiratory rhythm and that the respiratory signal is able to modulate locomotor rhythm.
the respiratory and locomotor circuits are functionally interconnected at the spinal cord level.
the spinal locomotor circuitry can modulate the excitability of spinal expiratory neurons, which is a prerequisite to coordinate the respiratory and locomotor activities.
The main takeaway from our work is that
respiratory neurons engaged in expiratory activity may be rhythmically modulated by the locomotor-related drive.
locomotor and respiratory networks share common spinal neurons, which could provide a substrate for the coordination of these two motor acts.
the locomotor drive to spinal respiratory neurons may play a crucial role in the coordination of locomotion and resiration during exercise.
